story: United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, collapsed without a deal after the European Union and other countries rejected a draft that made no mention of fossil fuels.
title: Climate talks collapse after draft omits fossil fuels
dek: United Nations climate talks in Antalya ended without a main deal after the European Union and others rejected a draft that never mentioned fossil fuels.
body:
United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, have ended without their main deal. After more than two weeks, and an overtime that made this the longest such summit on record, countries could not agree the so-called Antalya pact. It is the first time the annual talks have failed to produce an overall agreement since Copenhagen in 2009. Some smaller decisions did pass. The text meant to set the political direction did not.

The row was over a silence. Three years ago in Dubai, countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels. Early drafts in Antalya still pointed that way. Later drafts did not mention fossil fuels at all. Saudi Arabia and Russia refused the language. Turkey and Australia, the joint hosts, offered a trade: drop the words, and instead back a shift toward cleaner electricity. Oil producers could live with that. The European Union could not.

Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU, said the bloc would not sign a text that does not even mention fossil fuels. The United Kingdom, Panama, Norway and small island states joined that rejection. About 130 governments had wanted the words kept. Cutting emissions, they argued, is not the same as moving away from the fuels that cause most of them. A silent new text could make the Dubai promise look optional.

A Saudi negotiator, speaking for Arab states, said each country should choose its own path. Russia warned that cutting oil and gas supply before demand falls would mean shortages, higher prices and energy poverty, not lower emissions. China did not object to the weaker draft. Murat Kurum, the Turkish minister in the chair, said people should not be let down by a hang-up over one phrase. Australia’s Chris Bowen called the gap unbridgeable. These deals need consensus. Either side can stop the room, and both did.

Cash was the other unresolved fight. Poorer countries wanted firmer money to cope with heat, floods and failed harvests they did little to cause. The draft spoke of trying to triple adaptation finance by 2035, but without a clear baseline or a number anyone could collect. It also made room for carbon capture, technology that traps pollution so fossil fuels can continue. Critics say capture cannot replace using less coal, oil and gas.

## What still stands

The United States sent no official delegation, and President Donald Trump has rejected this process. Days earlier in Shenzhen, Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin said their countries planned to increase supplies of refined petroleum products. The planet is already about 1.4 degrees Celsius warmer than before industry, and a recent UN assessment says the 1.5-degree Paris limit will be overshot. On current policies, warming is heading nearer 2.8 degrees. Paris and Dubai still stand. Dozens of countries have signed an electrification pledge outside the failed text. The next summit is next year in Addis Ababa. A room that cannot name fossil fuels has not repealed physics.
